## Overview

Stacked on #64548, which replaces `reorg_kvcache` with an index-based row gather; please review that one first. Until it merges, this PR also shows its two commits. This PR adds the last three:

- `[Attention][DCP] Dequantize fp8 rows in the MLA DCP context row gather`
- `[Attention][DCP] Keep the MLA DCP context in fp8 through the all-gather`
- `[ROCm][DCP] Take the AITER MLA DCP context rows from the chunk metadata` (not fp8; can be dropped, see Details)

With decode context parallelism (DCP), a plain fp8 KV cache and an fp8 prefill query, the MLA chunked-context loop dequantizes each rank's cached rows into a bf16 (or fp16) workspace and all-gathers those rows across the DCP group. This PR keeps the rows in fp8 as stored through the local gather and the all-gather, and dequantizes them with the layer's `k_scale` in #64548's row-gather kernel. Everything after the gather (`kv_b_proj`, the K/V pack, attention, LSE merge) gets the same tensors as before.

## Claims

- Half the DCP context all-gather bytes (576 B per row instead of 1,152 B) and half the DCP context workspace.
- The prefill K/V are bit-identical to the default path whenever this path is on. The kernel dequantizes like `gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache` (fp32 product, rounded to nearest even), and every DCP rank holds the same `k_scale`, so dequantizing after the all-gather gives the same values as dequantizing before it. This holds for any `k_scale`; the previous revision of this PR required `k_scale == 1.0`.
- Off unless the backend opts in (`supports_fp8_dcp_context`, set only for `TOKENSPEED_MLA`), DCP > 1, the prefill query is fp8, the model dtype is bf16 or fp16, and every layer of the KV-cache group has an `fp8`/`fp8_e4m3` cache. Otherwise the default path runs unchanged.

### Performance

End-to-end results for this revision are being measured on top of #64548. They will be added here before this PR is marked ready for review.

Component: all-gather plus row gather per chunk, on one node of 4 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs (NCCL `all_gather_into_tensor`, CUDA events, median over 300 calls after 20 warm-ups, time of the slowest rank in each call; chunks built by `build_mla_chunked_context_metadata`, `k_scale` 0.37):

| DCP | Chunk | bf16 rows (#64548) | fp8 rows (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 66,304 rows, 1 request | 131.7 us | 92.8 us |
| 2 | 64,000 rows, 64 requests | 131.7 us | 92.8 us |
| 2 | 4,096 rows, 1 request | 47.8 us | 39.6 us |
| 4 | 66,304 rows, 1 request | 150.2 us | 105.1 us |
| 4 | 64,000 rows, 64 requests | 152.2 us | 107.2 us |
| 4 | 4,096 rows, 1 request | 45.7 us | 35.5 us |

The two paths' outputs were bit-identical on every rank and every chunk (12 chunks per DCP size).

<details>
<summary>Previous revision: end-to-end results (fp8 and the row reorganization together, older nightly)</summary>

Measured on the previous revision of this PR, which combined this change with what is now #64548, required `k_scale == 1.0` and ran on an older nightly. Kept for reference; it is not a measurement of this revision.

E2E on GB300, Kimi K3, one `vllm serve` instance on 2 nodes (TP8, DCP8, EP8, fp8 KV cache, `TOKENSPEED_MLA`, prefix caching), nightly image + that diff vs the same image without it. Two jobs in ABBA and BAAB order, 4 pairs, fresh server per segment. Metric: computed (uncached) prefill tokens per second; 95% CI is a t interval over the 4 pairs.

| Workload (concurrency 8) | main | that revision | Δ (95% CI) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: 130K-token prompts, 99% cached, 1K new tokens each | 9,350 | 8,884 | -4.5% [-17.6, +8.6] |
| B: 40K-token prompts, 76% cached | 40,003 | 40,484 | +1.2% [+0.3, +2.1] |
| C: 8K-token prompts, no cache (control) | — | — | +0.1% [-0.7, +0.9] |

- Workload A is noisy between segments: one main segment ran 15% faster than the other three main segments; in the job with tight segments that revision was +1.6%. We set a bar of +2% on workload A before the runs, and this result does not meet it.
- Outputs: 32 greedy requests over 8 long cached prefixes (logprobs 5) were identical between main and that revision in all 4 pairs and across nodes (32/32).
- GSM8K (2,638 answers per arm): main 0.9723, that revision 0.9727.

</details>

## Validation

Tests on one node of 4 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs (nightly image + this branch):

- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_dcp_fp8_context.py` (new):
  - the dequantizing row gather against `gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache`, bit for bit: every fp8 code including NaN, several `k_scale` values, bf16 and fp16 outputs, a latent width that is not a power of two, a NoPE layer with no rope part, int32 and int64 indices; and its input checks;
  - when the path turns on, including a group where any one layer lacks a plain fp8 cache;
  - the chunked-context loop handing the row gather the layer's `k_scale` and the default workspace dtype;
  - on two GPUs, with either DCP KV gather (NCCL and the direct symmetric-memory gather): the fp8 path feeds `kv_b_proj` and the prefill backend the same bytes as the dequantizing path, for several `k_scale` values updated in place, both model dtypes and both `kv_b_proj` input dtypes.
- #64548's tests (`tests/v1/attention/test_mla_dcp_context.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py`) pass. Two of them now also cover the dequantizing variant: the JIT warmup test and the DCP manager's warmup registration test. `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_mla_prefill_context.py` now also runs the DCP context loop on fp8 rows.
- CI: the single-GPU tests run in the existing V1 attention step. The two-GPU test (`-k matches_dequantizing_path`) is added next to #64548's two-GPU test in the nightly two-GPU "Distributed Features" step in `.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml`; that step is optional, so it does not gate PR CI.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/attention/test_mla_dcp_fp8_context.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_dcp_context.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_mla_prefill_context.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_mla_dcp_context.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py
```

Result: 351 passed, 18 skipped (ROCm-only), 0 failed. pre-commit, including mypy, passes on the changed files.

Not run locally: ROCm.

## Details

- **Workspace:** allocated in fp8, not viewed from a bf16 one, because the direct symmetric-memory KV gather sizes its buffers from the workspace dtype; both halve.
- **JIT warmup:** with a plain fp8 cache, the MLA DCP manager (see #64548) also registers the dequantizing variant of the row gather, because the builder picks the path per KV-cache group. When the group keeps the default path, that variant costs one small compile at startup.
- **No power-of-two requirement:** the previous revision needed power-of-two `kv_lora_rank` and `qk_rope_head_dim` because its kernel used them as block widths. #64548's kernel masks padded blocks, so that condition is gone.
- **Separate ROCm commit:** the ROCm AITER MLA DCP prefill now takes its context row indices from the chunk metadata (`context_row_indices`, cast to the int32 its fused gather takes) instead of building them with its own helper, which is removed with its test. It is not fp8 and was not run on ROCm; it can move to its own PR or be dropped.
- **Not covered end to end:** backends other than `TOKENSPEED_MLA` (they stay off; enabling one is a one-line opt-in after validation).
- **AI assistance:** Claude Code drafted the code, tests and description, and ran the measurements and tests above at my direction. I will review every changed line before marking this ready.

+"""Row gather for the MLA chunked-context loop under DCP."""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.warmup.jit_warmup_triton_helper import (
+    DispatchSpec,
+    TritonWarmupTensor,
+    triton_kernel_dispatcher_with_warmup,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+_BLOCK_ROWS = 32
+
+
+# A chunk's row indices start at any offset into the batch's indices, so the
+# kernel does not specialize on their alignment and one compile serves every
+# chunk. The k_scale pointer is read once and needs no alignment either.
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["row_indices_ptr", "k_scale_ptr", "num_rows"])
+def _gather_context_rows_kernel(
+    gathered_ptr,
+    row_indices_ptr,
+    k_scale_ptr,
+    latent_ptr,
+    k_pe_ptr,
+    num_rows,
+    LATENT_DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    ROPE_DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    LATENT_BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    ROPE_BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_ROWS: tl.constexpr,
+    DEQUANT: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    rows = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK_ROWS + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_ROWS)
+    row_mask = rows < num_rows
+    src_rows = tl.load(row_indices_ptr + rows, mask=row_mask, other=0)
+    src = gathered_ptr + src_rows.to(tl.int64)[:, None] * (LATENT_DIM + ROPE_DIM)
+    dst_rows = rows.to(tl.int64)[:, None]
+    if DEQUANT:
+        k_scale = tl.load(k_scale_ptr)
+
+    cols = tl.arange(0, LATENT_BLOCK)[None, :]
+    mask = row_mask[:, None] & (cols < LATENT_DIM)
+    latent = tl.load(src + cols, mask=mask)
+    if DEQUANT:
+        # The fp32 product rounded to nearest even, as the dequantizing cache
+        # gather computes it.
+        latent = (latent.to(tl.float32) * k_scale).to(
+            latent_ptr.dtype.element_ty, fp_downcast_rounding="rtne"
+        )
+    tl.store(latent_ptr + dst_rows * LATENT_DIM + cols, latent, mask=mask)
+
+    cols = tl.arange(0, ROPE_BLOCK)[None, :]
+    mask = row_mask[:, None] & (cols < ROPE_DIM)
+    k_pe = tl.load(src + LATENT_DIM + cols, mask=mask)
+    if DEQUANT:
+        k_pe = (k_pe.to(tl.float32) * k_scale).to(
+            k_pe_ptr.dtype.element_ty, fp_downcast_rounding="rtne"
+        )
+    tl.store(k_pe_ptr + dst_rows * ROPE_DIM + cols, k_pe, mask=mask)
+
+
+def _gather_context_rows_warmup_inputs(
+    *,
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+    kv_lora_rank: int,
+    rope_dim: int,
+    out_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
+) -> dict[str, object]:
+    # With out_dtype, the rows are fp8 and are dequantized into out_dtype.
+    inputs: dict[str, object] = dict(
+        gathered=TritonWarmupTensor(dtype, shape=(1, kv_lora_rank + rope_dim)),
+        row_indices=TritonWarmupTensor(torch.int64),
+        latent=TritonWarmupTensor(out_dtype or dtype, shape=(1, 1, kv_lora_rank)),
+        k_pe=TritonWarmupTensor(out_dtype or dtype, shape=(1, 1, rope_dim)),
+    )
+    if out_dtype is not None:
+        inputs["k_scale"] = TritonWarmupTensor(torch.float32)
+    return inputs
+
+
+@triton_kernel_dispatcher_with_warmup(
+    kernel=_gather_context_rows_kernel,
+    warmup_inputs=_gather_context_rows_warmup_inputs,
+)
+def _gather_context_rows(
+    gathered: torch.Tensor,
+    row_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    latent: torch.Tensor,
+    k_pe: torch.Tensor,
+    k_scale: torch.Tensor | None = None,

+    num_rows = row_indices.shape[0]
+    kv_lora_rank = latent.shape[-1]
+    rope_dim = k_pe.shape[-1]

+        k_scale_ptr=gathered if k_scale is None else k_scale,
+        num_rows=num_rows,
+        LATENT_DIM=kv_lora_rank,
+        ROPE_DIM=rope_dim,
+        LATENT_BLOCK=triton.next_power_of_2(kv_lora_rank),
+        # A NoPE layer has no rope part; the mask then skips the one-wide block.
+        ROPE_BLOCK=triton.next_power_of_2(max(rope_dim, 1)),
+        BLOCK_ROWS=_BLOCK_ROWS,
+        DEQUANT=k_scale is not None,
+        num_warps=4,
+    )

+def gather_dcp_context_rows(
+    gathered: torch.Tensor,
+    row_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_lora_rank: int,
+    k_scale: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    out_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,

+    """Copy the context rows out of the all-gathered DCP workspace.
+
+    With ``k_scale``, the rows are fp8 as the KV cache stores them and are
+    dequantized into ``out_dtype``: each value is widened to fp32, multiplied
+    by ``k_scale`` and rounded to nearest even, which is the arithmetic of the
+    dequantizing cache gather (``gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache``). Every DCP
+    rank holds the same k_scale, so dequantizing the rows after the all-gather
+    equals dequantizing each rank's rows before it.

+    Args:
+        gathered: Contiguous all-gathered rows ``[N, kv_lora_rank + rope_dim]``.
+        row_indices: Contiguous ``[C]``, the row of ``gathered`` that each
+            output row is copied from.
+        kv_lora_rank: Width of the latent part of a row.
+        k_scale: One-element fp32 tensor with the layer's k_scale, or None to
+            copy the rows unchanged. It is read on the device, so an in-place
+            update applies to the next call.
+        out_dtype: bf16 or fp16, the dtype to dequantize into. Given exactly
+            when ``k_scale`` is.
+
+    Returns:
+        The latent ``[C, 1, kv_lora_rank]`` and ``k_pe`` ``[C, 1, rope_dim]``,
+        both contiguous, in ``out_dtype`` if given, else in the dtype of
+        ``gathered``.
+
+    """
+    assert gathered.dim() == 2 and gathered.is_contiguous()
+    assert row_indices.dim() == 1 and row_indices.is_contiguous()
+    assert row_indices.dtype in (torch.int32, torch.int64)
+    assert row_indices.device == gathered.device
+    assert 0 < kv_lora_rank <= gathered.shape[1]
+    assert (k_scale is None) == (out_dtype is None)
+    if k_scale is not None:
+        assert gathered.dtype == current_platform.fp8_dtype(), gathered.dtype
+        assert k_scale.dtype == torch.float32 and k_scale.numel() == 1, k_scale
+        assert k_scale.device == gathered.device, k_scale.device
+        assert out_dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16), out_dtype
+    dtype = gathered.dtype if out_dtype is None else out_dtype
+    num_rows = row_indices.shape[0]
+    rope_dim = gathered.shape[1] - kv_lora_rank
+    latent = gathered.new_empty((num_rows, 1, kv_lora_rank), dtype=dtype)
+    k_pe = gathered.new_empty((num_rows, 1, rope_dim), dtype=dtype)
+    if num_rows:
+        _gather_context_rows(gathered, row_indices, latent, k_pe, k_scale)
+    return latent, k_pe
